content.title: 2025 NCAA men's basketball tournament: El Paso Times sports reporters predictions
content.text: March 18, 2025, 10:17 a.m. MTLiberty, Houston and St. John's are teams to watch in NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament.The 2025 NCAA men's basketball tournament tips off March 18 with a pair of First Four games in Dayton, Ohio, kicking off three of the most anticipated sports weeks in America.The 68 teams are aiming for spots in San Antonio for the Final Four, a field that includes a record 14 teams from the SEC. Five Texas teams are in the dance, including Rodney Terry's Texas team that plays Wednesday against Xavier in a First Four game.It all wraps up on April 7 with the men's 2025 national championship game. Here are some tips to help with the bracket.March Madness 2025: Felix Chavez predictionsThe 2025 NCAA men's basketball tournament will be entertaining as usual. As a graduate of the University of New Mexico, I think it's finally time the Lobos go far in the NCAA tournament. Led by explosive scoring guard Donovan Dent, I'm looking for the Lobos to be this year's Cinderella team. The Lobos are the No. 10 seed in the South and the Lobos won the regular season title in the Mountain West Conference and also own solid non-conference wins vs. UCLA and Virginia Commonwealth. I don't think the Lobos will win it all but I have them going to the Elite Eight.Arizona, Houston are teams watchOther notables I want to watch in the NCAA tournament include Arizona, the No. 4 seed in the East Region and Houston in the Midwest Region. Arizona is led, in part, by former El Paso Chapin High School star KJ Lewis, who has elevated his game to higher level this season. Houston, which is the top seed in the Midwest, plays aggressive defense and head coach Kelvin Sampson has made the Cougars a national power in recent years.Chavez's Final Four teamsAside from the St. John's Red Storm, thee other teams I like to reach the Final Four are Iowa State, Houston and Alabama.St. John's to claim the NCAA titleMy pick to be the NCAA champion is the Rick Pitino coached St. John's Red Storm. St. John's is 30-4 and the No. 2 seed in the West Region. Pitino took Providence, Louisville and Kentucky to the Final Four and he's made St. John's the kings of New York City once again. The Red Storm play with passion, no fear and have the best coach in America leading the way.Bret Bloomquist predictionsLiberty is the bracket busterLiberty is the underdog to pick in the first round. Conference USA has a good history in the first round (albeit not this iteration, which is in its second year) and the Flames are hot at the right time. They made a lot of noise in December, then again in February and March. Look for them to beat Oregon in one of those 5-12 upsets that happens every year.SEC isn't going to light it upThe SEC will be .500 in the first round. Did the conference really merit 14 bids? Is 6-12 in conference really deserving of a slot in the NCAA? Look for Texas to start things off right by beating Xavier in the play-in, but from there, the SEC goes 7-7.Bloomquist's Final Four teamsThe No. 1s are going to take half the Final Four, as Houston and Duke make it. So do St. John's and the No. 5 seed Memphis.Houston Cougars to win national titleHouston beats St. John's for the championship. The Cougars are an elite team getting hot at the right time. Their defense is the best in the tournament and that's the way to pick at that time of year. St. John's has been a sleeper all season, now is its time to make noise.Felix F. Chavez can be reached at fchavez@ekpasotimes.com; @Fchavezeptimes on X; Bret Bloomquist can be reached at bbloomuist@elpasotimes.com
